subject: Clarifying service-provider role, subprocessors & interstate transfer path (HavenHealth)
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@havenhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@havenhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA asks — service provider role + subprocessor visibility

Hi Mateo / Monica,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — HavenHealth is excited about Redwood's serving guarantees. Before we loop procurement, two tight questions from our legal/privacy team that will determine whether we proceed with a standard DPA or require a bespoke on-prem carve-out: 

1) Service provider vs processor language: we need explicit narrow-use language (no secondary use, no profiling outside the contract scope). Can you confirm Redwood's proposed clause and whether it will be limited to "providing inference services" only?

2) Subprocessor notice & emergency on-boarding: our policy requires 30 days notice for any new subprocessor; in emergencies we allow faster onboarding but with onshore fallback. Can you share Redwood's subprocessors and the proposed emergency-onboard process?

3) Interstate transfer / sale carve-outs: HavenHealth requires proof that telemetry/diagnostic logs will not be sold and that any cross-state transfers are limited to operation of the service. If there are any telemetry pipelines that persist PII, we need a dataflow diagram and retention schedule.

I've attached our suggested DPA redline template and a short mapping of the flow we expect. Can you confirm what evidence (SOC 2, dataflow map, attestation) you can provide and an initial turnaround for Redwood's redlines?

Thanks — Lena
Lena Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | HavenHealth

Attachments: haven_dpa_request.docx (docx)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@havenhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks — service provider role + subprocessor visibility

Lena — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the template. Quick triage from our side: 

- We can accept a narrow "Service Provider" (US state privacy) / "Processor" (DPA) use restriction limited to inference, logging for debugging, and fraud prevention. We will propose specific permitted purposes language rather than a blanket clause.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a core list (cloud infra + logging providers + monitoring) and a policy for emergency on-boarding that includes a 72-hour notice window followed by an onshore fallback commitment where feasible. We need to confirm which specific providers you consider unacceptable.

- Telemetry: we can produce a scoped dataflow map and retention table for diagnostic logs. We consider most telemetry aggregated and non-identifying, but we'll flag any pipelines that contain identifiers.

I'll loop in Legal (Marissa) for proposed redlines and Monica for the SOC/attestation packet. Proposed next steps: legal redline by EOD Monday (9/14), dataflow + SOC2 artifacts by Tuesday (9/15). Is that timing acceptable?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Account Delivery | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@havenhealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 15:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks — service provider role + subprocessor visibility

Lena / team — tagging in from Legal. We reviewed HavenHealth's template and propose the following novel compromise language and evidence package to keep this close to standard DPA while addressing your privacy team concerns: 

1) Permitted Purposes (new clause): "Redwood will process Customer Personal Data solely to provide inference services as expressly set out in the Agreement, to maintain and audit service performance, and to comply with legal obligations. Redwood will not use Customer Personal Data for model training, profile augmentation, advertising, or any purpose not reasonably necessary to deliver the contracted inference services."

2) Subprocessor notice & emergency onboarding: standard 30-day notice for planned subprocessors; emergency onboarding allowed with 72-hour operational notice and a written post-event report. In addition, Redwood will provide an onshore fallback plan (selected subset of infra partners with US-only processing) that HavenHealth can elect within 30 days of notice, subject to capacity and cost pass-through.

3) Telemetry & transfers: we will produce a scoped dataflow map and a per-stream retention schedule. For any stream that contains identifiers, Redwood will either pseudonymize before export or store within US-only regions per your preference. We will add an explicit "no sale" attestation paragraph for telemetry and diagnostics.

4) Evidence package: Redwood will deliver (a) SOC 2 Type II summary report (redacted), (b) scoped dataflow PDF, and (c) a signed attestation covering no-sale/no-training commitments.

5) Subprocessor list: enclosed in the attached redlines (Haven_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx). If HavenHealth has a blocker on any named provider, we can discuss bilateral mitigation (onshore alternative or contractual controls).

I made line-by-line redline suggestions in the attached. High-level commercial ask: if HavenHealth elects an onshore-only fallback, we will need to agree on an incremental fee to cover reserved capacity — we can capture that in a SLAs & fees exhibit.

Next steps: review our redline and evidence deliverables; if acceptable I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready packet.

Marissa Cole
Lead Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Haven_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

From: Lena Park <lena.park@havenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@havenhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks — service provider role + subprocessor visibility

Marissa — thank you, this is helpful and much closer to what we need. A few follow-ups from our privacy team after a quick read: 

- The "no training" language is required in explicit terms; can you add a single-sentence commitment that "Redwood will not incorporate Customer Personal Data into model training datasets or derivative models without Customer's prior written consent"?

- For emergency on-boarding: 72-hour notice is reasonable, but we need a follow-up mitigation window: Redwood must remediate or decommission the emergency subprocessor within 90 days or provide a documented justification and compensating controls.

- Regarding the onshore fallback fee: please provide a ballpark estimate or pricing mechanism (e.g., x% premium over baseline tokens or a flat monthly reserve fee) so procurement can budget.

If you can incorporate those items and send the SOC2 summary + dataflow by EOD Tuesday we'll route to procurement and aim to sign within a week.

Thanks — Lena

Attachments: none

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@havenhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks — service provider role + subprocessor visibility

All — quick confirm on timing and next steps. Per Marissa's draft I have: 

- Inserted explicit "no training" sentence as requested.
- Emergency subprocessor remediation: Redwood accepts a 90-day remediation/decommission requirement or documented business justification + compensating controls.
- Onshore fallback pricing: two options we can offer — (A) 15% premium on token usage routed to onshore pools, or (B) a reserved monthly capacity fee (example: $12k/mo for a small reserved pool supporting up to 50k tokens/min; exact sizing and pricing to be finalized with procurement). We will include both options in the packet and note that final pricing depends on peak qps and retention needs.

Attached: Haven_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx (redlines), dataflow-map-havenhealth.pdf (scoped), SOC2-bridge_report.pdf (summary). I've also prepared a DocuSign packet — link below — that includes our proposed DPA + SLA exhibit with both fallback pricing options. Please review and let us know if you'd like to swap the fallback fee structure before signing.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABCDEF-123456
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/HH-98765
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-haven-dataflow

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
